§6Cryogel§f

§aUltra-cold coolant. Without it, your DFC components melt into lava.§f

§bCryogel§f is a viscous liquid at §e-170°C§f, produced in the §bIndustrial Mixer§f from §e1,800 mB§f Coolant + Cryo Powder, yielding §e2,000 mB§f.

§6Uses§f:
§b• DFC Emitters§f, must be constantly cooled with cryogel or they melt into a lava source block immediately
§b• DFC Receivers§f, same requirement, both components consume §e20 mB/t§f

That's it. Cryogel exists for one purpose: keeping your DFC from destroying itself.

§cWARNING:§f Never run a DFC emitter or receiver without cryogel supply. They melt instantly, and if the beam has nowhere to go, you're looking at a catastrophic Fölkvangr field event that will crater your base.

§ePS:§f Set up automated cryogel production before you even think about building a DFC. You need a constant, uninterrupted supply during operation. AE2 or pipe systems handle this well.
